name: Full Body Foundation
summary: Build a steady lifting practice with three balanced full-body workouts.
description:
## Who it suits

Start with movement you can repeat confidently. Two working sets per movement keep early sessions approachable while covering a squat, hinge, press and pull across the rotation.

## The rotation

Complete two or three sessions in a week. Each training position is followed by a rest position; add extra recovery whenever technique or readiness needs it. The six positions are not weekdays.

## Progression

Add repetitions within the range before increasing load. Keep roughly three reps available and use the lighter option when learning a movement.

## Before you lift

- Begin with light practice and gradually heavier warm-up sets for the first compound movements. Warm-ups are separate from listed working sets.
- Rest longer when breathing or technique has not recovered; rest guidance is not a timer requirement.
- Prescribed RIR is a target, not your actual report. Record actual effort only if you choose.

> Reduce load or stop when a movement causes pain. Seek qualified guidance when learning unfamiliar lifts.

name: Foundational Barbell Strength
summary: Learn the barbell basics through three distinct, alternating full-body sessions.
description:
## Who it suits

Practice controlled squat, hinge and pressing patterns without testing maximums. The third session uses a lighter squat variation and paused press to reinforce consistent positions.

## The rotation

Train three nonconsecutive days per week. This is an ordered three-workout rotation, not three consecutive calendar days. Allow at least 48 hours between sessions.

## Progression

Use small load steps only after every planned repetition is repeatable with stable technique. Hold load when reps or recovery decline; targets are guidance, not a promise of weekly increases.

## Before you lift

- Begin with light practice and gradually heavier warm-up sets for the first compound movements. Warm-ups are separate from listed working sets.

name: Upper / Lower Strength & Size
summary: Four complementary workouts pair strength practice with measured accessory volume.
description:

## The rotation

name: Push / Pull / Legs
summary: A flexible eight-position rotation balances compound work and focused accessories.
description:
## Who it suits

Two push, pull and leg sessions vary their emphasis while retaining familiar movements. Isolation work follows the compounds, with moderate volumes that can be reduced when recovery is limited.

## The rotation

Six training positions and two rest positions form an eight-day cycle if followed daily: approximately 5.25 sessions per week. Add rest to use three to six sessions weekly without skipping the workout order.

## Progression

Progress reps before load, retaining about two reps in reserve. Do not shorten recovery merely to fit a calendar week.

name: Classic Body-Part Split
summary: Five focused sessions distribute chest, back, legs, shoulders and arm work.
description:

name: Classic Physique — Six Day
summary: Six complementary workouts revisit chest/back, shoulders/arms and legs.
description:

name: High Intensity, Low Volume
summary: Low set counts and deliberate recovery for lifters comfortable judging effort.
description:
## Who it suits

This compact rotation suits experienced lifters who can distinguish hard, controlled repetitions from compromised technique. Optional failure intent is limited to a final isolation set, never all movements.

## The rotation

Three sessions and six rest positions make a nine-day cycle, about 2.33 sessions per week if followed daily. Keep the two rest positions between workouts and take longer when needed.

## Progression

Stop compound work with roughly one or two good reps available. The isolation failure intent is optional and means acceptable-technique failure; skip it when unsure or poorly recovered. Add reps first, then a small load step.

## Before you lift

- Begin with light practice and gradually heavier warm-up sets for the first compound movements. Warm-ups are separate from listed working sets.
- Rest longer when breathing or technique has not recovered; rest guidance is not a timer requirement.

name: Powerbuilding
summary: Major-lift practice and supplementary muscle-building work across four sessions.
description:
## Who it suits

Keep heavier lifts early, then use moderate-repetition assistance to build training exposure without treating every accessory as another maximum-strength test.

## Progression

name: Strength 5×5
summary: An original three-session approach using one five-by-five main lift each day.
description:
## Who it suits

Five sets of five are reserved for one main movement per session. Assistance uses fewer sets so the method does not turn every lift into a high-volume strength test.

## The rotation

Train three nonconsecutive days per week. The six-position rotation includes rest after each workout; add another rest day as needed rather than accelerating the cycle.

## Progression

Warm up through gradually heavier, low-fatigue practice sets that do not count toward the five working sets. Increase the main load by a small step only after all 25 reps are controlled; repeat the load when they are not.

summary: Efficient full-body muscle exposure for three available training sessions.

description:

name: Functional Strength
summary: Measurable strength practice across bilateral and unilateral movement patterns.
description:
## Who it suits

Build familiarity with controlled squats, hinges, presses and pulls alongside unilateral practice. Progress is measured through performed reps and loads, without promises of injury prevention or guaranteed sport performance.

## The rotation

Use three to four sessions per week and add recovery between demanding sessions. The four positions include one prescribed rest; extra pauses are expected, so the rotation is not a four-calendar-day deadline.

## Progression

Choose loads that leave two or three reps available and keep unilateral technique consistent on both sides. Progress reps before load; use the lower-performing side to guide the session.

## Before you lift

- Begin with light practice and gradually heavier warm-up sets for the first compound movements. Warm-ups are separate from listed working sets.
